sentences.text: Today is the equipment list: what the law says must be on your boat before a paying passenger steps aboard.
We start where every boarding officer starts.
You need a Coast Guard approved wearable life jacket for every person aboard, in the right size.
And because you carry passengers for hire, they must be the offshore type, traditionally called Type one, with the most flotation.
An adult jacket on a six-year-old doesn’t count, and it doesn’t work.
They must be readily accessible and in good condition.
So are they legal if they’re still sealed in plastic under a locked seat?
Readily accessible means a passenger can get one in seconds.
Newer jackets carry performance-level labels instead of Types, and the older ones stay legal while they’re serviceable.
And you need a throwable device, usually a ring buoy, ready at hand.
